purpose: Teach no-code and low-code building as real product development that still requires requirements, data design, security, testing, deployment, ownership, and exit planning.
staffSummary: Build M39 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Decide whether a no-code or low-code tool fits a bounded prototype and what controls are required before using real utility data. The learner must leave with a usable no-code prototype decision and test plan, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A useful prototype is built in a day, but nobody can explain where the data resides, who administers access, how changes are tested, or how the utility can leave.
learnerDecision: Decide whether a no-code or low-code tool fits a bounded prototype and what controls are required before using real utility data.
analogy: Prefabricated building parts can speed construction, but the site, foundation, inspections, and ownership still matter.
learnerOutcomes: Explain No-Code and Low-Code Building: Lovable, Bolt, Replit, Vector Shift in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish prototype, production system, no-code, low-code, generated code, integration, administration, lock-in, and exit without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Keep tool capabilities, prices, export options, hosting, and terms dated. Do not place restricted utility data into an unapproved builder.
Create a usable no-code prototype decision and test plan with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give No-Code and Low-Code Building: Lovable, Bolt, Replit, Vector Shift one clear learning job inside Building AI Systems.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the no-code prototype decision and test plan.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Decide whether a no-code or low-code tool fits a bounded prototype and what controls are required before using real utility data.
Name the no-code prototype decision and test plan as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
requiredWorkProduct: no-code prototype decision and test plan
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete no-code prototype decision and test plan, and names the next accountable action.
scopeBoundary: Keep tool capabilities, prices, export options, hosting, and terms dated. Do not place restricted utility data into an unapproved builder.
